newsitem.title: USA: Yeltsin offered not to target China -- Japan.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin offered not to target China -- Japan.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin said in was time to stop targeting nuclear missiles at China as well as Japan during a meeting on Friday with Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto, a senior Japanese foreign ministry official said.
The official, who briefed reporters on condition of anonymity, said Yeltsin's remark was ambiguous and would have to be taken up in a later meeting.

While Yeltsin in the past has offered to stop targeting missiles the United States and Europe, his comment on Friday was the first time he had specifically included the major Asian countries of China and Japan.

The official said Yeltsin told Hashimoto, "As an act of goodwill, the missiles have been de-targeted from such countries as the United States, Britain, Germany and France. Now is the time to completely de-target missiles from countries like Japan and China."
The official added, "What he meant was quite unclear to us. It was impossible to understand what he meant."
Yeltsin is in Denver to attend most sessions of the annual summit of the Group of Seven leading industrialised countries starting later on Friday.
